title: Labeling edge cases scratchpad
content:
Scratchpad: labeling edge cases + cleanup notes
Owner: Ava Patel (personal notes)
Context: prepping a short guideline doc for labelers and a small set of canonical examples we can push into the onboarding bundle. Mostly rough, will refine after convo with Jordan/Marco.

Goals:
- Collect hard-to-label examples we've seen in user-generated text (UGT) set.
- Propose heuristics for consistent labeling and minimal rules for adjudicators.
- Draft a few canonical samples to include in training / QA tasks.
- Note cleanup scripts ideas (regexes, filters) for obvious noise.

High-level labeling principles (working):
1) Prefer conservative labels when uncertain: if intent/meaning unclear, mark as "ambiguous" instead of guessing a sentiment or category.
2) Keep labels orthogonal: don't mix sentiment + intent unless the task explicitly requires multi-label.
3) Document every special-case rule in a single place (Confluence PROJ-423).

Edge cases and proposals
-----------------------------------
1) Short single-token responses: "ok", "nope", "lol", ":)"
- Problem: Very little signal, often depends on thread-level context.
- Proposal: If the sample is isolated (no preceding turns), label as "insufficient_context". If part of thread and preceding message shows clear intent, inherit label from thread context.
- Example: "lol" (isolated) -> insufficient_context.

2) Mixed-language segments (code-switching): "I loved it, pero no me gustó la interfaz"
- If annotation target is sentiment: consider majority-language sentiment weighting. If split sentiment across languages, mark as "mixed_sentiment" or provide separate per-segment labels.
- Quick heuristic: if >70% tokens in language X, label by that language's interpretation.

3) URLs or handles as proxies for content: "Check this out: https://youtu.be/xyz123"
- We should avoid labeling based on linked content unless the task includes link following. Mark as "external_reference". Optionally flag for follow-up dataset enrichment (crawl + summarize).

4) Repeated filler and spammy content: long repeated characters or tokens: "!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!!" or "buy now BUY NOW buy now"
- Auto-label rules: if repetition threshold (e.g., >5 identical tokens consecutively) -> mark "spam_or_noise" and exclude from main training pool. Keep a small sample for model robustness tests.

5) Overlapping labels: profanity + sarcasm + humor.
- Example: "Oh sure, your code is *so* brilliant (not)"
- Rule: prioritize label ordering for downstream tasks: 1) safety (profanity/hate) 2) intent (instruction/ask) 3) affect (sarcasm/sentiment).
- Adjudication note: if safety label present (HATE/PROFANITY), that dominates for content-policy pipelines.

6) Implicit references and coreference: "They ruined it again" without antecedent.
- When antecedent is missing in snippet, mark as "requires_context". For datasets derived from conversations, try to surface previous 1-2 turns to label.

7) Numeric ambiguity: "Charge was $0.00, weird" vs "Charge was 0, weird" (thousands separator / localization)
- For entity labels, include normalization step in cleanup (map localized digits, strip currency symbols) before labeling.

Canonical examples (for onboarding spreadsheet)
- Example A: "meh" -> insufficient_context
- Example B: "I paid but never got access :(" -> intent: support_request; sentiment: negative
- Example C: "Check this out: https://imgur.com/a/abc123" -> external_reference
- Example D: "buy now buy now buy now" -> spam_or_noise
- Example E: "I hate that they disabled the feature for no reason" -> sentiment: negative; safety: none (unless target expresses protected class)

Quick adjudication rubric (for 2nd-pass reviewers):
- Step 1: Does the text contain policy-sensitive content? If yes, tag and stop.
- Step 2: Is the text clearly an instruction or support request? If yes, label intent.
- Step 3: If sentiment is required, can sentiment be determined without additional context? If not, mark ambiguous.

Cleanup scripts / heuristics (ideas):
- URL-only messages: regex ^https?://\S+$ -> auto-tag external_reference and optionally call out for crawl.
- Excessive punctuation sequence detection: /([!?\.\-])\1{4,}/ -> spam_or_noise.
- Token-length filter: if len(tokens) < 2 and token in set(["ok","lol",":)",":D","nah"]) -> insufficient_context unless conversation context available.
- Non-printable characters: normalize and drop non-UTF chars; flag file encoding issues.

Open questions / TODOs
- What threshold should we use to drop spam from training vs keep for robustness? Jordan proposed 1% of training set but need empirical check.
- Mixed-language labeling: do we want per-segment labels or a single label with language tag? Action: ask Marco for labeling UI constraints.
- Do we want an explicit "requires_context" label or prefer an "insufficient_context"? (Naming matters for downstream filtering).
- Build a small 200-example adjudication set with high variance edge cases for labeler calibration.

Action items (short):
- [ ] Create 200-example calibration set (Ava to draft 50, Jordan 75, Marco 75) by 2026-03-20.
- [ ] Add URL-only auto-tag pipeline to quick-clean script and test on 5k random samples. (PR: gh:dataset-cleanup#87)
- [ ] Write short labeling note for onboarding (1 page) summarizing 5 top-edge rules.

Notes to self: keep everything short for labelers. People skim long docs. Use examples > rules where possible.

Conversation refs: slack #dataops thread Feb 12 (link in Confluence), tag Jordan/Kim for UI question.

End of scratchpad.
